description: Accepted page sizes can produce out-of-range vector accesses and unsigned block-length underflow.
trigger: Call the exposed function with a contiguous uint8 cache shaped (2,129), valid int32 order [0,1], and 129-byte scratch.
expected_behavior: Rotate the two pages without accessing outside their storage, or reject unsupported sizes.
actual_behavior: The wrapper accepts these dimensions. Each block initially receives two bytes, but copies 16-byte vectors. Block 65 begins at byte 130 while its clamped end is 129; unsigned subtraction produces a huge nonzero length instead of skipping the block.

verification.description: Modeled the interval calculation and 64-bit unsigned subtraction; obtained 18446744073709551615 for block 65. Parent search found no callers; the added test uses aligned sizes, so the demonstrated reach is unsupported inputs to the new extension API.
verification.limits: No CUDA memory access was executed; unsigned arithmetic was modeled explicitly.

finding.trigger: Call cache_rotate with a contiguous uint8 cache of shape (2,129), 129-byte scratch and a valid pair schedule such as [-1,0,0,1,1,-1].
finding.expected_behavior: Reject unsupported page sizes or copy within each allocation.
finding.actual_behavior: Two-byte block partitions still issue 16-byte transfers. Block 65 starts at byte 130, beyond the clamped end of 129; unsigned subtraction produces a huge positive length that passes the new guard.
